persona.systemPrompt: You are a helpful voice assistant. Keep all answers under four sentences. Do not use markdown, bullet points, or numbered lists. Do not begin a sentence with "Certainly" or "Of course". Spell out abbreviations when reading aloud. When asked where you looked something up, answer from the results earlier in this conversation.

prompts.webSearchFailed: (A web search for this question failed, for example because the device is offline. The app already told the user that. Say what was true as of your training data, using words like "até onde sei pelo meu treinamento". Never say it is true today, and never put today's date on it. Keep it to two sentences.)

prompts.toolNotAllowed: Not done: the user did not ask for this. Do not mention it; just answer what the user said.
prompts.toolResultNote: (This is the tool's result, not a message from the user. Now answer me in one short sentence.)
prompts.noToolRetry: Reply to what I said above, in plain words.

router.comment: Decides what a turn needs before the model answers. Layers, cheapest first: rules (exact commands only), semantic (the closest route by example sentences), classifier (trained on the device from the same examples), llm (the loaded model answers one word), then relevance (web results that don't match the question are dropped). Learning: sentences the model decided, searches that found nothing relevant, and router.feedback corrections become examples. Without an embedding model (configure {router: {embeddingModel: path}}) word overlap is used, with the lexical* thresholds. default: what to do when nothing decides: "rules" (webSearch.rules), "none", or a route id.

llm.question: (Before you answer: what kind of message is this? Reply with one of these English words only: search if it is a question that needs current information from the internet, such as news, weather, sports, prices or who holds an office; food if I am telling you something I ate or drank, even a food you have never heard of; correction if I am correcting something you logged; remove if I am asking to remove something I logged or saying I did not eat it; total if I am asking how many calories I have had today; personal if I am telling you about my own life, plans, family or feelings; knowledge if it is a general question you can answer yourself; chat if it is small talk.)
llm.dataToolMinScoreComment: The model's pick of a tool that changes data is taken only when it is also the router's top candidate with at least this score; otherwise no tool.

memory.comment: What the assistant remembers about each user (speaker) across conversations. types: how each kind of memory lives (lifetimeDays: short-term, afterExpiry: what it becomes) and is used (inject always = every prompt; relevant = when the turn's words match; guidance = how to behave while it lasts; checkIn = asked once per day). rules: patterns that capture memories from the user's words ({1} = first group, :title capitalizes). profiles: how much memory to use; the app picks one per model with configure({memory: {profile}}) and can override any field.

grief.guidance: The user is grieving. Be warm and gentle, keep answers soft, and don't repeat condolences every turn.

spelling.comment: Letters spelled out in a row ("O for Oscar, F for Frank"): the first letters of the words make the word (speech recognition mangles the letters but not the words). replace: what the memory rules see, "(spelled: ofer)"; forModel: what the model gets in place of the spelling, "Ofer (O-F-E-R)".

memory.fieldsComment: fields: values the app needs right. key = the memory key (rules with that key feed the field); spelling: off | allowed (a spelled value, "O for Oscar, F for Frank", wins over what speech recognition heard) | required (only a spelled value is accepted); verify: read it back and keep it after a yes; required: the model asks for it until it is known and verified (again after askAgainMinutes, default 60), and once it is, nothing is added to the prompt; mentions: a spelled word in a message matching this goes to this field (checked in order, so the more specific field first); answer: optional pattern for a direct answer after we asked (group 1). fieldPrompts ask/spellHint go to the model; spell/readBack/confirmed/retry are said as they are, without the model.
